current.text: Caleb Wilson is a rookie. The Bulls drafted him with the No. 4 overall pick.
He is in Chicago's projected starting five with Josh Giddey, Norman Powell, Matas Buzelis and Nic Claxton.
Experts expect him to be the second-best rookie this season.

He is expected to be a low-usage option as a rookie, at about 30 minutes and 20 percent usage or less. Powell, Giddey and Buzelis are expected to use more of the ball, and the Bulls are not expected to push his offensive role.
In summer league he averaged 22 points and 7 rebounds on 37 percent usage and shot 42 percent on 8 threes per game, but his shooting fell off as summer league went on.

His summer league shooting is seen as partly fool's gold. He may shoot only about 30 percent from three this season, his early efficiency is expected to be rocky, and his early value should come from defense.
One expert thinks he should take more threes this season.
Experts call his ESPN rank (56 to 66) too high. A top 100 season would be a good result, and the 80s is a fair range for him in category leagues.

Experts disagree on his draft spot in the 80s. One calls pick 89 good value and a perfect spot. Another is uneasy taking him at pick 84, and a third has not drafted him anywhere because of the uncertainty.
Pairing him with Zach Edey takes away much of Wilson's upside.
Chicago is projected to be a bad team. One expert predicts 32 wins and another calls it probably a bottom-six team.
Tiago Splitter is Chicago's new head coach. He replaces Billy Donovan and is expected to push young players out of their comfort zones.
The Bulls should play a fast, up-tempo transition style. A lineup with Claxton, Wilson and Giddey is expected to have terrible spacing.
Chicago has 15 back-to-backs, one below the maximum. Its fantasy playoff schedule is 3-3-4 games (10 total) with our March 28 end date.

durable.text: His fantasy value comes from defensive stats and rebounding: blocks, steals and rebounds. Blocks are his best category for a forward.
Shooting is his weakness. He is a poor free throw shooter, and his percentages are uncertain.
He was not a high-usage player in college and rarely shot threes there.
He is not expected to help in assists. One expert worries about tunnel vision and does not think he can pass.
He is a good finisher and athlete.
Over the long term his game probably leans more to defense than offense, though the gap should narrow.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues because his value comes from defensive stats.

note: Wilson is a defense-first rookie forward. His blocks (+1.8 z vs forwards) and rebounds (+1.3) carry him, and his FT% (74.8 percent) and threes are mild drags. Experts put him in the 80s overall, which fits a mid-to-late pick in our 144-player draft at about Yahoo's 11 USD value. ESPN's 5.5 USD average cost and rank 57 are seen as too high, and our league did not draft him last season. He suits blocks-and-rebounds builds that can absorb a weak FT%. Early in the season, check his usage next to Powell, Giddey and Buzelis, and whether his summer league three-point volume carries over.
